newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crude premiums dump, market oversupplied.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crude premiums dump, market oversupplied.

text.p: The North Sea crude market was thrown into turmoil on Tuesday when a cargo of Brent traded at a differential to December almost $1 below trade one week ago.
A cargo of Brent due to load in November 5-7 range traded on Tuesday at December Brent -43 cents, some 37 cents below trade on Monday and almost $1 below trade last week.
Last Wednesday an early November cargo traded at November Brent +10 cents when Nov/Dec was trading at +35 cents.
"It (the Brent differential) has moved almost as much as the outright price. People are chock-a-block with crude and this (weakness)is going to last a while," one refiner said.
"Crude needs to move out of the region -- look at the Mediterranean and West Africa. They are full as well," he added.

Differentials for sweet and sour crudes alike in these regions have fallen off over the past few days. Notably Russian Urals, which traded a week ago at dated Brent -60 cents, was now offered at -80 cents with few bids seen.
Mediterranean refiners said they bought enough crude to cover themselves up to at least mid-November already and could not hold any further stocks.
"We bought when the gas oil brought the margins to the highs and can't buy any more," one Mediterranean refiner said.
Traders also said that Brent had been kept artificially high last week by one trader who either kept (from the paper chains) or bought seven of the early November Brent cargoes.
"Last week was unbelievable. It was more than manipulation. If that happened on any other market it would be a big thing - on this market nothing is done. Nothing can be done," one refiner said.
"This is a reaction to the market being kept artificially high last week and fundamentally we are very weak," another commented.
